summary.headline: Lumax Auto Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% y-o-y to INR 1,556 crore, with PAT up 50% to INR 117 crore; FY27 growth guided to 20-25%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,500 crore for the first time in a quarter, up 35% y-o-y and 14% q-o-q, with EBITDA of INR 228 crore (14.7% margin, broadly flat y-o-y). H1 FY27 revenue reached INR 2,919 crore (+34%), EBITDA INR 434 crore (+42%, margin 14.9%, up 90 bps) and PAT INR 215 crore (+64%). Management raised its full-year revenue outlook to 20-25% growth (near INR 6,000 crore), with H2 growth of 15-20%, and said the order book rose to INR 1,879 crore. Margin dilution in Q2 was attributed to input-cost pass-through lag of about one quarter.

segments.name: Advanced Plastics (incl. IAC)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue rose 45% y-o-y to INR 1,655 crore from INR 1,138 crore; IAC is about 60% of the division. Order book INR 834 crore. Contributes 44% of total order book.

segments.name: Mechatronics
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 45% y-o-y to INR 177 crore from INR 122 crore; order book INR 512 crore. Management says margins are in line with the overall company. Contributes 27% of order book.

segments.name: Structures & Control Systems
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 24% y-o-y to INR 476 crore from INR 380 crore; order book about INR 150 crore. Contributes 8% of order book.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 9% y-o-y to INR 234 crore from INR 216 crore; Q2 growth was 11%. Non-lighting category weakened as input-cost increases were passed on.

segments.name: Alternate Fuels (Greenfuel)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 30% y-o-y to INR 220 crore from INR 170 crore; order book INR 379 crore. Contributes 20% of order book. Nashik facility began production in Q3 FY27 for M&M.

segments.name: Lumax Industries (LIL) wiring business
segments.commentary: Reported H1 revenue flat y-o-y because one product line moved to in-house supply by LIL; management says like-for-like growth is about 25-30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now guided at 20-25% y-o-y, implying roughly INR 6,000 crore; H2 FY27 growth expected at 15-20% y-o-y due to higher FY26 base.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance unchanged; management expects current margins to be sustained for the rest of the year.
FY28 absolute EBITDA target of about INR 1,000 crore reaffirmed.

North Star: 20% revenue CAGR FY25-FY31, with EBITDA margin moving toward 20% over 5-7 years; FY31 revenue aspiration about INR 11,000 crore. Organic CAGR of about 20% now seen as achievable if industry momentum holds.
Margin ambition of a further 100-200 bps over the next few years, toward 17-18%.

Capex guidance for FY27 around INR 300 crore, including greenfield expansions in Mechatronics, Advanced Plastics and Alternate Fuels; SOP expected in H2 FY27. Effective tax rate about 25%; minority interest about 11% of PAT.
capex_capacity: Capex capitalised in H1 FY27 was INR 60 crore; full-year capex guided at about INR 300 crore.

Board approved (24 Oct 2026) a new Mechatronics plant at Manesar, Haryana, with capex of about INR 150 crore funded by debt and internal accruals; commissioning in two phases from Q3 FY28, peak turnover about INR 500 crore.

Greenfuel Nashik facility began production in Q3 FY27 (ferrule-less tubes, fittings, receptacles) for M&M; Maruti Suzuki firm orders also won. Capacity expected to be significantly utilised by M&M and Maruti over about 2 years.
IAC Chakan Plant IV is in SOP phase; product launches expected around December 2026 to January 2027. Efficiency gains from centre-of-competence concept to be quantified after launch.
demand_pricing: Management cites industry Q2 FY27 production growth (SIAM): overall +19% y-o-y to 106 lakh units; PV +25% to about 17 lakh; 2W +17% to 81 lakh; 3W +25% to about 4.5 lakh; CV +34% to 3.5 lakh. Growth expected to moderate in H2.

Inflation: input costs (crude-linked polymers, electronic parts, freight, rupee) are rising. Most cost increases are passed to OEMs with about a one-quarter lag; management says pass-through is complete, with a 30-40 bps EBITDA margin dilution in Q2.
Order book of INR 1,879 crore: about 14% to execute in FY27, 59% in FY28, 27% in FY29; about 85% is new business. EV and CNG together are 29% (CNG 20%, pure EV about 9%); future technologies 22%.

Content per vehicle: about INR 70,000-75,000 per PV and INR 20,000-22,000 per 2W; about 50% of PV content is in IAC; Greenfuel about INR 5,000-8,000 per vehicle. Mechatronics is about 20% of PV content; expected to rise about 10% in 2-3 years.
Aftermarket growth target of 15-20% over a 3-5 year horizon, despite weak H1.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance being raised after 34% H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management now expects FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% y-o-y (about INR 6,000 crore), versus the earlier implied 12-14%. H2 growth is expected at 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins face pressure in Q3, and is the FY28 EBITDA target of INR 1,000 crore on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through lags about one quarter, so margins dilute by a few bps. It remains confident of the FY28 INR 1,000 crore EBITDA target and of sustaining current margins in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% North Star revenue CAGR (FY25-FY31) still realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is now more confident of about 20% organic CAGR if industry growth holds. Inorganic growth could push it higher. The base year is FY25.

qa_highlights.question: Who develops the Body Control Module (BCM), and is it reported in standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: BCM is a build-to-print standalone revenue stream since SOP in July 2026, with a INR 250 crore order book. Technology comes from a large Japanese electronics component maker, not a JV; it is reported under Mechatronics across standalone and subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV component strategy and the Aftermarket outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: EV focus is narrowed to 3-5 products, with active SOPs targeted for 2028-2030 and possible inorganic routes. Aftermarket grew 11% in Q2 and 9% in H1; the 15-20% target is over 3-5 years.

risks_watch: Input-cost inflation (crude-linked polymers, electronics, freight, rupee) and the one-quarter pass-through lag, which dilutes margin by 30-40 bps in Q2.
Festive-season demand sustainability and H2 moderation, with H2 growth guided at 15-20%.
Aftermarket weakness in non-lighting products, with H1 growth at 9%.
Mechatronics BCM ramp faces global competition and is in build-to-print phase; the Manesar plant is due Q3 FY28.
Dependence on JV partners for technology and IP (Mechatronics: about 75% of IP via JVs). One JV (with JOPP of Germany) was dissolved amicably in Q2.
Geopolitical conflict in the Middle East and energy price volatility, flagged by management as key uncertainties.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and guidance, with the FY27 outlook raised. Cautious on input costs and H2 moderation. Evasive on specifics for Chakan IV efficiency gains and the BCM counterparty name, which were not disclosed.
key_quotes: Q2 FY 27 revenue stood at INR 1,556 crore, up by 35% y-o-y and 14% quarter-on-quarter (q-o-q).
we can expect the full-year growth to be somewhere in the region of 20%-odd, if we compare from FY 26.
we are quite confident of delivering the absolute guidance of EBITDA for FY 28, which was always at about INR 1,000 crore EBITDA.
It is standalone revenue for Lumax Auto Technologies, and we are extremely proud of it.
